name: bing_search_camoufox
description: Bing web search (organic results). Fixed bing.com host; country routed via cc= and language via setlang= (derived from the locale). Materializer lowercases `country` for cc= and derives a language code for setlang= from the locale. Every organic href is a click-tracking wrapper — bing.com/ck/a?...&u=a1<base64url> — so `links` read straight from href pointed at bing.com on EVERY row: a field 100% populated and 100% useless, which no fill-rate check can see. The destination is recovered by pulling the `u=a1` capture and base64-decoding it. An href that is not a wrapper yields null rather than a mangled value. ENGINE: Camoufox, fingerprint_profile=windows_on_host — a Windows claim over this host's real AMD GPU vendor. Windows rather than the honest Linux because measurement put an honest Linux claim at 15 and 23 retries against 1 and 8 for Windows (see src/browser/fingerprint_profile.py). MEASURED 2026-08-27 (n=2 per locale, 6 runs per engine, research/preset_audit_dual_engine_2026_08_27.json): 6/6 runs returned data on both engines; this variant returned 10 rows on every locale, against 10 on us and ru but only 2 and 5 on de for bing_search_chromium, whose short runs also raised row_alignment_mismatch and returned an ordered subset of the rows this variant got from the same German SERP. ROW-COUNT CAUSE, corrected 2026-08-28 fix round 2 (reproduced in tests/presets/test_bing_search_row_alignment.py): for the two raw captures actually in hand (bing_camoufox_de.html classic, bing_chromium_de.html Copilot -- both complete, well-formed final pages, not truncated mid-render snapshots), it is NOT the wait strategy an earlier read of this audit blamed for those two specific pages -- both twins ship identical wait_until=domcontentloaded / no wait_for_selector / timeout_ms=30000, and the other engine returned a full 10 rows on us and ru in the same run. Bing draws one of two different SERP layouts per session: the classic layout (ten li.b_algo, nothing else) and a Copilot/generative-answer layout that, on the capture in hand, renders 3 li.b_algo AND promotes its rank-1 organic result OUT of the list entirely into div.b_wpt_bl, a card inside the answer widget reusing the exact same title/link/snippet template as li.b_algo (verified: it decoded to the SAME destination, title and snippet as li.b_algo's own rank-1 on the classic capture). A first version of this fix widened the selector for the layout gap but missed this promoted card, undercounting by one on every Copilot draw shaped like the capture in hand. The selector now also matches div.b_wpt_bl h2 a[href*='u=a1'] -- an h2-scoped anchor carrying the organic redirect prefix, not the container class alone -- because the SAME answer widget has three OTHER div.b_wpt_bl siblings (a YouTube card, a topic-filter strip, a Gesponsert ad card) that carry real u=a1- or aclk-shaped hrefs of their own but have no h2 at all, PLUS a constructed regression case proving u=a1 itself is load-bearing rather than redundant with the h2 gate: an ad card whose title anchor DOES sit inside an h2 (a shape Bing's own ad templates already use elsewhere on this same page) is excluded only because its href is a bare aclk redirect, not u=a1. Verified end-to-end with extract_fields against the real captures: a clean 10/10/10/10 on the classic capture and a clean 4/4/4/4 on the Copilot one (rank 1 = the promoted PCMag card, matching the classic capture's own rank 1), zero warnings both times. If a page ever renders BOTH the promoted card AND leaves its own rank-1 result in li.b_algo -- unobserved, but not excludable, see the historical-runs paragraph below -- this preset emits that result twice; co-occurrence is not currently guarded against. Separately, li.b_ans.b_top (Bing's generated-answer prose) is excluded, but not because its anchors are empty -- it holds 22 real anchors decoding to 5 distinct external hosts (forbes.com, pcwelt.de, chip.de, faz.net, produkte-im-test.de), all numbered citation footnotes. Its own three h2's, checked directly, contain zero anchors between them, which is the actual, narrower reason an h2-scoped selector cannot reach them. li.b_ad.b_adBottom's three nested ads (a visible 'Gesponsert' badge, an aclk -- not ck/a -- redirect whose u= value lacks the organic a1 prefix) remain excluded the same way they always were. NOT resolved by this fix, and NOT confirmed to be the same defect: the historical 2-row and 5-row runs (research/preset_audit_dual_engine_2026_08_27.json entries 30-31), including the row_alignment_mismatch itself (titles=2/links=2/snippets=1 and titles=5/links=5/snippets=4 -- always exactly one snippet short). Their raw HTML was never kept (the audit record stores a slimmed row count, not markup), so neither their layout NOR the wait-strategy account of them can be confirmed or ruled out -- and the one piece of entry 31 that CAN be checked argues against assuming it hit the same mechanism as the capture in hand: it was collected under the OLD selector (li.b_algo h2 a[href^='http'], which cannot reach div.b_wpt_bl), yet its own links[0] is https://www.pcmag.com/picks/the-best-laptops -- meaning PCMag was reachable there as an ordinary li.b_algo, not promoted out of the list the way it is on the capture in hand. Entry 31's 5-row, one-snippet-short composition is therefore at least as consistent with a page snapshotted mid-render (5 of 10 classic slots painted so far, CHIP's caption not yet among them) as with any Copilot-layout account of it. Track entries 30-31 as open and their layout as unobserved, not as confirmed instances of the mechanism this fix addresses. Also not asserted: that which layout a session draws correlates with engine. The two raw captures in hand are one Copilot-layout observation on Chromium and one classic-layout observation on Camoufox -- n=1 each. The historical runs' layouts are unobserved (previous paragraph), and entry 31's own composition argues against counting it as a second Chromium/Copilot data point rather than for it. No number is put on any correlation, and no engine preference is asserted for de in either direction. The ck/a decode holds on div.b_wpt_bl's promoted card exactly as it does on li.b_algo (same u=a1 shape) on both layouts and both engines; Bing's ad redirect (aclk) uses a different, undecodable u= shape that this pipeline correctly leaves null rather than mistaking for a destination. MEASURED 2026-08-28 (retest of the same twenty presets through the same harness after the five audit fixes; n=2 per locale, 92 runs, research/preset_audit_dual_engine_2026_08_28.json): THE COPILOT ROW FIX COULD NOT BE TESTED: Bing did not serve the Copilot layout to any exit on 2026-08-28. A dedicated probe that sends this preset's exact request but splits the shipped union selector into its two halves found div.b_wpt_bl container count 0 on 18 of 18 runs (3 runs x 3 locales x both engines), so the promoted rank-1 card the widened selector exists for was never on the page -- and a clean run on the classic layout is not evidence about it. What the probe does establish is that the widening costs nothing where it does not apply: shipped rows == li.b_algo rows on 18/18. This variant's own audit rows: 10/10/10/10/10/10, 0 warnings. But 2 of those 6 runs (both ru) answered a DIFFERENT QUERY at HTTP 200 with a full 10 rows -- Microsoft Community forum threads on one, the npm package 'nocache' on the other -- so read a 10-row bing run as a well-formed page, never as a relevant one. UPDATE 2026-09-04 -- THE `u=a1` PREFIX IS NO LONGER PRESENT ON EVERY RUN, and the gate above is widened accordingly. Camoufox loads uBlock Origin on every launch (`add_default_addons()` is called unconditionally inside camoufox's own `launch_options()`; `exclude_addons` is the only way out, see CAMOUFOX_DISABLE_UBO), and uBO's default-enabled Privacy list carries `bing.com##+js(href-sanitizer, a[href*="bing.com/ck/a"], ?u /^a1(.*)$/ -base64)`, whose scriptlet does `elem.setAttribute('href', hrefAfter)`. So on the Camoufox twin the organic anchors arrive ALREADY DECODED -- uBO performs exactly the unwrap this preset's own post_process performs, only earlier. Measured live 2026-09-04, one variable, everything else equal: 10 anchors either way, 10 carrying `u=a1` with uBO excluded and 0 with uBO loaded. That silently broke the field: `bing_search_camoufox` went from 0 selector misses on 2026-09-02 to 4 of 6 on 09-03 while its Chromium twin stayed at 0 in the same run, and it surfaced as "required selector not found" on a page that had loaded fine, because titles/links share ONE selector keyed on `u=a1` while the container-scoped snippets/result_blocks kept matching 10 rows. Nothing in the repo triggered it: uBO is downloaded at first browser LAUNCH, not at image build, so a container recreate adopts whatever filter lists upstream ships that day. The anchor gate now reads `&u=a1` OR `?u=a1` OR `not(contains(@href,'bing.com'))`, on all four fields at once, and the two branches are disjoint because a wrapper is always on bing.com. The ad exclusion `u=a1` used to carry alone is now carried in two places instead: an ad's `aclk` href is still on bing.com so the new branch rejects it (uBO's rule selects on `ck/a` and leaves `aclk` alone), and `links`' post_process ends in `null_if_regex` on `bing\.com`, so anything that reached the column without a destination being recovered is nulled rather than shipped as a plausible link. `links` now runs `unwrap_param(u, base64url, a1)`, which passes a value it cannot unwrap THROUGH rather than nulling it -- that pass-through is what lets one column serve both shapes.
